assistantAssessment.agreement: Source leads should seed discovery, not define its ceiling. Reward resourceful investigation that produces consequential evidence across relevant channels and returns to earlier hypotheses.
assistantAssessment.remainingDisagreement: A's claim that two reports of the same teaser reinforce a franchise interpretation remains unsupported. User's positive view of the investigative direction does not establish independent provenance or a justified initial ranking.
assistantAssessment.benchmarkGap: The current authored excerpt exercise chiefly tests handling supplied evidence. It cannot demonstrate actual independent discovery, media analysis execution, search breadth or tool competence. Initial B scores remain preserved under their original scope, not promoted into comprehensive discovery excellence.
assistantAssessment.interpretationBoundaries: Character prominence, story, intended audience and business motives are questions or hypotheses to investigate, not facts inferred solely from teaser prominence. Do not require a particular franchise, journalist or platform, or assume named sources have relevant information.

proposedCriteria.name: Adaptive source discovery
proposedCriteria.success: Seek sources likely to distinguish live hypotheses beyond the initial leads; follow productive references and document negative or inaccessible leads when consequential.
proposedCriteria.avoid: Counting platforms, queries or tool calls as quality; demanding every listed channel.

proposedCriteria.name: Claim-level provenance
proposedCriteria.success: Trace a specific claim to its earliest accessible source, date, firsthand basis and corroboration; distinguish independent information from repeated speculation regardless of source fame or anonymity.
proposedCriteria.avoid: Treating popularity, anonymity, reputation or repeated reporting as sufficient proof.

proposedCriteria.name: Discriminating visual comparison
proposedCriteria.success: Compare identifiable details in inspected frames with dated candidate references, include mismatches and plausible counterexamples, and show why a resemblance does or does not distinguish candidates.
proposedCriteria.avoid: Treating generic horror imagery or a similar silhouette as franchise identification, or claiming footage was inspected when only a thumbnail was available.

proposedCriteria.name: Relevant strategic synthesis
proposedCriteria.success: When useful to the user's question, connect sourced catalog, audience and positioning evidence to clearly labeled story or commercial hypotheses, with alternatives and evidence that could change the interpretation.
proposedCriteria.avoid: Mandatory business speculation on every task, invented buyer data, or presenting inferred corporate intent as an announcement.

proposedCriteria.name: Productive nonlinear continuation
proposedCriteria.success: A new clue can reopen or redirect a branch; revisions preserve human notes and prior uncertainty. Pause when marginal evidence is weak and resume when a specified informative source becomes available.
proposedCriteria.avoid: Endless search, forced guesses, or rewriting earlier hypotheses as established facts.

benchmarkDesignFollowup.historicalCase: Do not claim independent historical discovery from unrestricted current web search: later reveal contamination and model memory remain known limitations. A broader historical retrieval corpus would need date-eligible documents, provenance, distractors and legitimate alternate investigation paths.
benchmarkDesignFollowup.generalization: Pair historical reasoning calibration with a contemporary open investigation for actual source-finding assessment. Do not silently replace or expand the frozen case during comparison.
benchmarkDesignFollowup.canvasAssessment: Later browser evaluation should show inspected media, specific comparison details, attributed claims and revisable hypotheses as individual native objects. Explanatory text alone cannot establish this.
